  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37641v1</id>
    <title>Algebraic fiberings of right-angled Coxeter groups on bipartite cone graphs</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T17:54:48Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37641v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.37641v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We study systems of moves and states in the sense of [JNW21] on certain bipartite graphs, and the associated homomorphisms from the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups to $\mathbb Z$. We give examples of right-angled Coxeter groups whose graphs do not satisfy the legal system criterion, but contain finite index right-angled Coxeter subgroups whose graphs admit legal systems. We also provide a family of examples of graphs without legal systems, where no sequence of the considered graph operations yields a graph with a legal system. Moreover, we show that for a bipartite graph and an orbit of non-empty states under the bipartite system of moves, the associated homomorphism from the commutator subgroup of the right-angled Coxeter group to $\mathbb Z$ has finitely generated kernel if and only if the system is legal.</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37490v1</id>
    <title>Rank functions, $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions and class numbers</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T16:16:56Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37490v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.37490v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>If $F$ is a number field and $F = F_0 \subset F_1 \subset F_2\subset \cdots$ is a tower of Galois extensions with $\mathrm{Gal}(F_n/F)$ cyclic of order $p^n$, K. Iwasawa gave a closed formula for the growth of the $p$-part of the class number of $F_n$ whenever $n$ is large enough. We present a new proof of this formula, obtained by reinterpreting its summands in terms of Sylvester matrix rank functions on the Iwasawa algebra $Λ$ without resorting to the classification of finitely-generated $Λ$-modules up to pseudo-isomorphism.</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37462v1</id>
    <title>On a problem of A. N. Skiba and L. A. Shemetkov concerning $S_n$-closed subformations of a one-generated formation</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T16:00:40Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37462v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.37462v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Throughout this paper, all groups are finite. Let $\mathrm{form}(G)$ denote the formation generated by a group $G$. A formation $\mathfrak{F}$ is said to be $S_n$-closed if every subnormal subgroup of every group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to $\mathfrak{F}$. A. N. Skiba and L. A. Shemetkov posed the problem of proving that $\mathrm{form}(G)$ has only finitely many $S_n$-closed subformations for every group $G$ (Problem 14.81 of the Kourovka Notebook). In this paper we propose a negative answer to this problem. We prove that for the group $G_0=(\mathrm{SL}_2(5)\rtimes C_2)\times\mathrm{SL}_2(5)$ of order 28800, where $C_2$ acts on $\mathrm{SL}_2(5)$ by an outer automorphism, the formation $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ has an infinite strictly descending chain of $S_n$-closed subformations. The main tool is a family of central-valued multilinear maps, defined for every group in $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ by its outer actions on its components; their vanishing is preserved under taking epimorphic images, subdirect products and subnormal subgroups. The members of the chain are separated by central quotients of the groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(5)^{2^d-1}\rtimes C_2^d$, $d\geq 2$. Using Burichenko's description of the lattice of subformations of $\mathrm{form}(\mathrm{SL}_2(5)\rtimes C_2)$, we also prove that every non-empty $S_n$-closed subformation of $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ is generated, as an ordinary formation, by a single group, and that the set of such subformations is countably infinite. Finally, we determine the intersection of the chain and give an explicit generator of it.</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37399v1</id>
    <title>Representation and abelianization growth, particularly along expanding sequences</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T15:17:46Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37399v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.37399v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We study two obstructions to a finite group $G$ having a generating $d$-tuple whose Cayley graph has spectral gap at least $ε$. Lubotzky and Weiss proved that such a gap forces $\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, the largest order of the abelianization of a subgroup of index at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_ε(dk))$, while de la Harpe, Robertson and Valette proved that it forces $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)$, the number of irreducible complex representations of degree at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_ε(dk^2))$. We show that the first bound implies the second, and in fact implies it with $k^2$ replaced by $k\log k$. For this, we prove that every finite $d$-generated group satisfies the inequality $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)\leq\exp((d-1)k\log k+O(dk))\cdot\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, regardless of its spectral gap. The leading term $(d-1)k\log k$ is attained by powers of alternating groups, and it disappears for groups without large alternating sections. The proof reduces to counting the finite primitive subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbf{C})$, and we show that there are at most $\exp(O(\log^4m))$ of them up to conjugacy and scalars. Wigderson asked whether $k^2$ in the second bound can be lowered to $k$, so our result answers his question up to a logarithm. We do not know whether the logarithm is actually needed. For powers of alternating groups, the natural candidates, we show that a spectral gap keeps the number of factors a fixed power below the maximum allowed by $d$-generation, and that random generators have spectral gap tending to $0$ already for superpolynomially many factors.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37334v1</id>
    <title>Irrationality of the conjugacy growth on Heisenberg groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T14:41:24Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37334v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.37334v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We demonstrate that the conjugacy growth series for the Heisenberg groups $H_n(\mathbb{Z})$ is never algebraic, irrespective of the generating set. This makes progress towards the conjecture that all finitely presented groups that are not virtually abelian have irrational conjugacy growth series. Contrary to the group $H_3(\mathbb{Z})$, where the conjugacy growth is $n^2\log(n)$, the conjugacy growth of the other Heisenberg groups is polynomial, making these groups the first known nilpotent groups where the irrationality does not follow from the asymptotic growth.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37291v1</id>
    <title>Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T14:14:52Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37291v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.37291v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37042v1</id>
    <title>On $π$-nilpotencies of finite skew braces</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T11:13:40Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37042v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.37042v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let $π$ be a set of primes. We extend the theory of left and right $π$-nilpotency in skew braces beyond the nilpotent type setting, and introduce the study of central $π$-nilpotency for finite skew braces. We investigate the relationships between these three notions, and a characterisation of central $π$-nilpotency in terms of chief factors is also established. This leads to the introduction of the $π$-Fitting ideal of a skew brace, for which we prove a local analogue of Fitting's theorem and provide a description in terms of centralisers of chief factors. Finally, we introduce the $π$-core of a skew brace and investigate its relationship with $π$-ideals and central $π$-nilpotency.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36497v1</id>
    <title>Failure of the congruence Hasse principle for commutators in orientable surface groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-27T01:54:38Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36497v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36497v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Ghosh, Meiri and Sarnak showed that the commutator equation over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfies a profinite local to global principle, and that for a prime $\ell\equiv\pm1$ mod $5$ it fails for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell])$ with a reciprocity obstruction. We extend the failure to surface groups. For the genus-$2$ surface group $Γ_2$ we construct an explicit representation $ρ:Γ_2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, where $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1}{10}]$, whose quotients modulo the maximal ideals are the full groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ except in residue characteristic $3$, where the quotient has order $24$. For every $k\ge2$ the word $[a_1,b_1]^k$ is not a commutator in $Γ_2$, while its image is a commutator in every one of these quotients. The same holds for every surface group $Γ_g$ with $g\ge2$.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.NT" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36401v1</id>
    <title>Degree-one cohomology of metacyclic $2$-groups: a low-bit dichotomy</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T23:29:58Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36401v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36401v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We study the subalgebra generated by degree-one mod-$2$ cohomology for metacyclic $2$-groups $G=\langle a,b\mid a^{2^α}=1,\ b^{2^m}=a^c,\ b^{-1}ab=a^r\rangle$ with unique normal forms, where $α,m\ge2$ and $r\equiv-1\pmod4$. Presentation compatibility forces $c=0$ or $2^{α-1}$ and $G^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong C_2\times C_{2^m}$. If $c\equiv0\pmod4$, the degree-one-generated algebra is $\mathbb{F}_2 [x,y]/(y^2,x^2+xy)$, a four-dimensional algebra shared by the four nonmodular types of Aaboun--Zekhnini. The unique exceptional case $α=2$, $c=2$ is modular and has infinite-dimensional degree-one algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y]/(y^2,x^2y)$. The regular algebra is PBW, Koszul, universally Koszul, and strongly Koszul, whereas the modular algebra is not Koszul. We realize the regular algebra by inflation from the common quotient $C_4\rtimes_{-1}C_4$ and identify its quadratic dual with the characteristic-two Jordan plane. For the inversion tower $C_4\rtimes_{-1}C_{2^m}$, we give uniform presentations of the full mod-$2$ cohomology rings and determine the kernels and images of inflation in every degree. Their direct limit yields the continuous cohomology ring of $C_4\rtimes_{-1}\mathbb Z_2$. We also record an arithmetic consequence for Galois groups arising over cyclotomic $\mathbb Z_2$-extensions of real quadratic fields.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.RA" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36394v1</id>
    <title>Realizing graph automorphisms as geometric symmetries of straight line drawings</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T23:19:27Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36394v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36394v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Given a finite graph $G$, we characterize the automorphisms and automorphism groups of $G$ that can be realized as geometric symmetries and symmetry groups of straight line drawings of $G$ in the plane. In doing so, we correct a previous version of this characterization from the literature. As an application, we show that the graphs recently constructed by the first two authors to disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which have orders $16{,}464^k$ for each positive integer $k$, are the first known vertex-transitive graphs with no non-trivial realizable geometric symmetries. We also construct infinite families of graphs that exhibit all possible kinds of geometric symmetry.</summary>
